summary.intent: Investigate the someguy sidecar state on staging, diagnose IPNS performance issues, and upgrade Kubo to v0.40.0 to improve IPNS reliability.
summary.outcome: Discovered someguy's IPNS endpoint is completely non-functional (hangs indefinitely) while provider lookups work fine; upgraded Kubo from v0.34.0 to v0.40.0 locally with all 83 E2E tests and 5 load test scenarios passing with zero errors; PR #321 created with a release-triggering commit type.

repo: The docker/ directory (docker-compose.staging.yml, Caddyfile, etc.) is generated during CI and copied to the VPS — it is committed to the repo at /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/docker/ but not deployed via git.

DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL defaults to https://delegated-ipfs.dev in the delegated-routing client fallback (apps/api/src/ipns/delegated-routing.client.ts line 24); staging overrides it to http://someguy:8190 via .env.staging and the deploy workflow.
Someguy was intended to replace delegated-ipfs.dev as part of Phase 19: IPNS Resolution Improvement, documented in .planning/phases/19-ipns-resolution-improvement/.
Delegated routing publish is fire-and-forget since PR #308 — failures are warnings only and don't fail the API response.
The ThrottlerModule is hardcoded (10 req/s, 100 req/min) with no NODE_ENV=test relaxation; tests must send X-Throttle-Bypass header with THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET.
SDK E2E tests have no .env file and require THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET to be set inline or added to avoid 429 failures.

code.finding: Fallback default URL is https://delegated-ipfs.dev when DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env var is not set
Kubo image version pin — updated from v0.34.0 to v0.40.0
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 is injected at deploy time, which resets any manual .env.staging edits on the server

workflow: Someguy v0.11.1 provider lookups (/routing/v1/providers/) work correctly but IPNS endpoints (/routing/v1/ipns/) hang indefinitely — the two APIs have different reliability characteristics.

When all 5 vitest load test scenarios run concurrently, the sustained-load scenario (5 min duration) causes 522 Cloudflare errors that bleed into other scenario results — run scenarios in isolation for clean baselines.
Load test 'errors' can be misleadingly high: the harness records success:false for any thrown exception including SDK-side failures unrelated to HTTP status codes.
The deploy workflow injects DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL into .env.staging, so manually disabling someguy on the server by editing .env.staging will be overwritten on the next deploy.
Release Please uses squash merge commit titles for release notes — commit type matters (chore vs build) for triggering releases.

friction: The 'disable someguy' change from a prior session was never persisted — the deploy workflow reset .env.staging on every deploy, making the manual change invisible in git history.
NODE_ENV=development in .env overrides the shell environment variable, so NODE_ENV=test must be set in the .env file itself, not just the shell, for NestJS ConfigModule to pick it up.
Load tests initially appeared to have ~95% error rates but this was misleading — the errors were SDK-level IPNS failures due to someguy's broken IPNS endpoint, not HTTP failures from the API.
vitest --testPathPattern='mixed-workload' accidentally matched 'sustained-load' too, causing all 5 scenarios to run when only one was intended.
Someguy's IPNS endpoint hangs indefinitely (never returns) rather than returning an error, causing the API to waste 30s (3 retries × 10s timeout) on every publish attempt.
open_items: Post-phase-19 performance baseline collection against staging is deferred until the Kubo v0.40.0 upgrade (PR #321) is deployed to staging.
Someguy's IPNS endpoint is broken — decision on whether to remove the someguy sidecar entirely or switch DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL back to delegated-ipfs.dev on staging is pending.
The TEE Worker still uses delegated-ipfs.dev directly and is not routed through someguy — this was noted but not addressed.
Load test THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET is not configured in the SDK E2E test environment — currently requires manual inline env var injection.
